counts: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. 28 of the 55 are hidden on PlayStation until earned.
guideNote: Every guide below is written in our own words for this guide, from the trophy's official description and the counts PlayStation tracks. Grand Theft Auto VI released 19 November 2026, so no guide below has been checked in the game yet: where a place or step is not pinned down by the official description, the guide says so instead of guessing.
list: The official 55 trophies, as PlayStation publishes them (names, descriptions and grades as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles, 18 Nov 2026 — the two agree on every name, description and grade).

sources.label: Exophase — official trophy list (names, descriptions, grades)
PSNProfiles — trophy list and the counts PSN tracks

trophies.guide: The platinum lands the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap: story first, then stranger strands, activities, collectibles, crime feats and the one-off moments, with 100% completion last. If a trophy is still missing, the tracker above shows exactly which kind it belongs to, so work the remaining kind, not the whole list at random.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first story mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn and it cannot be missed — just play the story from the start. If you are already past the opening, the trophy should already be in your collection; a missing one here means the mission was never completed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end. Chapter trophies unlock automatically when the chapter's final mission is done, so there is no special requirement — follow the story missions in order and this pops at the chapter break. Story chapters cannot be missed: finishing the chapter is the only condition.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its end, the same way as Chapter 1. The trophy is tied to the chapter, not to any single mission inside it, so any route through the chapter's missions earns it. It unlocks at the chapter break — if it has not popped, a Chapter 2 story mission is still open.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its end. Like the other chapter trophies it unlocks automatically at the chapter break, with no extra objective. Use the pause menu's story progress to check which Chapter 3 missions remain if the trophy is still locked after a long session.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 4 to its end. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, and it unlocks at the Chapter 4 break. Once it pops, the story's final mission is all that stands between you and the gold story trophy — but do not rush it: several missable strand finales and one-off moments are best done before the finale (see the Missables tab).
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the story's final mission. This is the gold story trophy and it unlocks automatically on completion, so it cannot be missed — but the moment before it is the point of no return for anything missable. Before starting the final mission, check the Missables tab: finish the contact finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), the stranger strands and any one-off moment trophies first, because the game may not let you return to them afterwards.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. The trophy is named for the mission itself, so finishing the mission is the whole requirement. It is flagged missable because it is tied to a single named mission: play it when it comes up in the story and confirm the trophy pops at the mission's end, rather than planning to come back to it later.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete Breakfast Run while you play it — do not assume a replay re-awards it.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. As with the other named-mission trophies, the requirement is simply to finish that mission. Flagged missable because it belongs to one mission only: do it when the story offers it, and check the trophy pops before moving on to the next chapter.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete The Cartel Heist while you play it.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. The trophy unlocks when the mission ends, with no extra objective named in the description. Flagged missable for the same reason as the other named-mission trophies: it is earned inside one mission, so finish the mission when the story reaches it.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete Child's Play while you play it.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The trophy is the mission's completion reward and nothing more. Flagged missable because it is tied to a single named mission: play Headliners when it appears in the story and confirm the pop at the end of the mission.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete Headliners while you play it.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. The trophy unlocks on mission completion. Flagged missable because it belongs to one named mission only — finish VCIA Takedown when the story offers it instead of leaving it for a later replay.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete VCIA Takedown while you play it.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Like the other named-mission trophies it pops when the mission ends. Flagged missable because it is tied to that one mission: play it when the story reaches it, and treat the mission's end screen as the confirmation.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to one named story mission. Complete Operation Savage Glory while you play it.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% in the game's completion stat, shown in the pause menu. This is the long grind behind the platinum: story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the crime feats all feed the percentage, so it is best treated as a checklist rather than a trophy to chase directly. Work through the tracker kind by kind — the remaining unearned trophies are a good proxy for what the completion stat is still missing — and use the in-game completion breakdown to find the last few percent. It cannot be missed: everything that counts toward it can be done after the story.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, long airtime and the like — across Leonida. PSN tracks the count, so the trophy pops the moment the 250th stunt registers. There is no single place to do them: build them into ordinary driving, taking jumps and threading traffic wherever you travel, and the count climbs without a dedicated grind. Use the tracker's counter below to log your running total, since the game does not show it on the trophy itself. It cannot be missed: stunts can be done anywhere, at any time.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type in the game at least once — PSN's count says there are 9 types. The description does not name them, but the game's activities are the ones this guide's activity trophies cover: shooting range, stunt driving, races, drone races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and hunting. Work through those nine, one session each, and the trophy pops when the last type is tried. It cannot be missed: every activity stays available after the story.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks the count to 42. Go challenge by challenge and treat each as its own small skill test: learn the target pattern and the weapon it asks for before chasing gold, and use the tracker's counter to note how many golds you hold. The challenges are repeatable, so a silver or bronze on a first attempt costs nothing but another try. It cannot be missed: the range stays open after the story.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks the count to 14. Each location is its own race, so this is a tour of the drone-race map rather than one repeated event: win one race at a location, move to the next, and tick it off in the tracker. Learn each course's line before pushing for the win; the races are repeatable, so a lost race is just a retry. It cannot be missed: every location stays available after the story.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word different matters: repeating one easy race twenty times does not count. Race across Leonida's events and tick each new win off in the tracker until 20 distinct races are won. Pick the vehicle class that suits each race rather than forcing one favourite onto every course, and expect the later races to be the harder ones. It cannot be missed: races stay open after the story.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival the trophy names — find a fishing challenge against him and out-fish him. The description names no place, so use the fishing spots the game marks and the challenge prompts it offers; the challenge itself is the event, not a hidden location. If a first attempt fails, the challenge can be retried — it cannot be missed, since fishing stays available after the story.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish a full game at an arcade machine anywhere in Leonida. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or the one you enjoy most; the trophy pops when the game ends, win or lose, as long as it is completed rather than abandoned. It cannot be missed: arcades stay open after the story.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Stranger and contact strands unlock as you meet people across Leonida — follow Andy's missions whenever they appear until the strand ends. Flagged missable as a caution: a contact's final mission is the end of that strand, so finish it before the story finale rather than assuming the strand stays open afterwards.
trophies.missableNote: Final mission of Andy's strand. Finish it before the story finale to be safe.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand by completing his final mission. Like the other contact finales, this is the last mission of one person's strand — play Kenton's missions as they appear until the strand closes. Flagged missable as a caution: finish it before the story finale rather than assuming the strand stays open afterwards.
trophies.missableNote: Final mission of Kenton's strand. Finish it before the story finale to be safe.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Work through Billy's missions as they appear across Leonida until the strand ends. Flagged missable as a caution: a contact's final mission closes that strand, so finish it before the story finale rather than assuming it stays open afterwards.
trophies.missableNote: Final mission of Billy's strand. Finish it before the story finale to be safe.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the Strangers & Freaks of the state. Each strand is a small chain of missions for one stranger; finish eight of them and the silver pops. Explore the map's stranger markers between story missions rather than leaving them all for the end, and count your finished strands in the tracker — the contact finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands too, so they count toward the eight. It cannot be missed: stranger strands stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Play Randy's missions as they appear until the strand closes. Flagged missable as a caution: finish it before the story finale rather than assuming the strand stays open afterwards.
trophies.missableNote: Final mission of Randy's strand. Finish it before the story finale to be safe.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand by completing his final mission. Work through Tyrone's missions as they appear until the strand ends. Flagged missable as a caution: finish it before the story finale rather than assuming the strand stays open afterwards.
trophies.missableNote: Final mission of Tyrone's strand. Finish it before the story finale to be safe.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 18. Each spot is a place to sit and meditate; visit all of them and the trophy pops at the last one. The description names no spots, so use the tracker's counter to log each one as you find it and sweep the map region by region rather than wandering at random. It cannot be missed: meditation spots stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a single, named creature rather than ordinary wildlife. Bret's strand will point you at the hunt; follow his missions until the unique animal is the objective, then track and take it down. The description names no species or place, so do not guess one: let Bret's strand set the target, and treat the hunt as a strand mission rather than a free-roam chore. It cannot be missed: the strand stays available after the story.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — collect the cards of three full sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida, so this is a long sweep: pick up cards as you travel, keep the sets you are closest to finishing in the tracker notes, and trade or hunt down the last cards of a set once you know which ones are missing. The trophy pops when the third set is complete. It cannot be missed: cards stay collectible after the story.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — PSN tracks the count to 100. WAiNK is the game's photo-style activity: find its marked locations across Leonida and use it at each one. Sweep the map region by region and log the running count in the tracker, since the count itself is the grind and the locations are the only thing to find. It cannot be missed: every location stays available after the story.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's assorted side challenges, from driving and combat to world activities. There is no fixed list in the description, so take them as they come: every challenge the game offers counts, and fifty of them is a long tail rather than a single session. Check the in-game challenges list for the ones nearest completion and finish those first; the tracker counter below keeps your running total. It cannot be missed: challenges stay open after the story.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while playing with your partner, then escape the heat. Build the wanted level with your partner beside you — four stars means the police response is heavy, so plan the escape before you earn the stars: a fast car, a route out of the search area, and somewhere to break line of sight. The trophy pops once the stars clear with your partner still with you. It can be retried as often as you like, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level — the tricky part is the second half: you must keep the heat the whole way through. Pick three shops close together, plan the route between them before the first robbery, and keep moving so the wanted level never drops to zero between shops. If the level clears, the chain breaks and you start the three again. It can be retried freely, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or ride in 100 distinct vehicle models across Leonida. Every new model you get into counts, so variety is the method: try the cars, bikes, boats and aircraft you pass rather than sticking to one favourite. The tracker counter below keeps your running total. It cannot be missed: vehicles stay discoverable after the story.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode. Set it up rather than hoping for it: find a spot with at least five enemies close together, enter Combat Focus with a full meter and a weapon that drops targets fast, and chain the five takedowns before the meter runs out. A failed attempt costs nothing but another try, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — leave VCIA by air without a ticket or a flight plan, in the game's own cheeky phrasing. In practice that means taking an aircraft from the airport and getting airborne: find a plane on the VCIA apron, get in and take off. Expect airport security to object, so be ready to move fast once you are on the tarmac. It can be retried, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Deal with Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke, not an instruction, so the honest reading is this: find a Rhino tank in the world and do something with it, most plausibly take one for a drive or take one down. The game's military presence is the place to look, and the trophy's name (a play on a hot tank) suggests being inside one rather than just near one. It cannot be missed: tanks and the places that hold them stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery, not a smash-and-grab. Plan it like one: scout the store, go in quiet, keep out of sight lines and alarms, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. Any detection fails the attempt, but the attempt can be retried, so it cannot be missed. If the first plan trips an alarm, change the approach rather than the target.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — five full vault jobs, each one ending in a clean getaway. Treat each vault as its own heist: plan the entry, grab the take and have the escape route ready before you go in, because the escape is part of the trophy. The tracker counter below logs each vault you finish. It cannot be missed: bank vaults stay robbable after the story.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run routes across Leonida — intercept one, stop it, take its cargo and get away clean. The escape is part of the trophy, so have a fast vehicle and a route out of the search area ready before you strike. It can be retried as often as needed, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — PSN tracks the count to 52. The trophy pops when the last undiscovered area is entered, so this is a map-completion sweep: drive, fly and walk through every region until the area counter stops climbing. Use the in-game map's area names as your checklist and the tracker counter below for your running total, and save the remote corners — the islands and the far north — for a dedicated sweep. It cannot be missed: areas stay explorable after the story.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN tracks the count to 9. Each gang runs its own operations somewhere in Leonida; hit one operation per gang and the trophy pops at the ninth. Work gang by gang and tick each one off in the tracker so you know which gangs are still untouched. It cannot be missed: gang operations stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — find a bar or vendor on Ocean Beach with a view of the water, order a cocktail and take it in. This is a moment trophy, not a grind: go to Ocean Beach, find somewhere serving drinks with a view, and the trophy pops when the moment lands. It cannot be missed: Ocean Beach and its bars stay open after the story.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through a showroom's glass and out the other side, the way the old games taught us. Pick a showroom with a clear run at the glass, build speed inside and keep going through the window rather than stopping at it. It can be retried, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — play a game of bowling there and see it through to the end. The alley is named in the description, so head to Kolt & Associates, start a game and finish it; the trophy pops when the game is complete. It cannot be missed: the bowling alley stays open after the story.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal — the description is deliberately vague, so the honest reading is that this pops from a story beat about the partnership between the two leads, most likely a mission or cutscene moment that the game flags as the partnership going public. Play the story and it should come on its own; if it has not popped by the finale, check the mission list for a partnership mission still open. It is flagged as a story moment, not a grind, and it cannot be missed by free-roam play.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count to 500, so this is a long tail of decisions across the game, not one big choice. Every decision the game offers counts toward the 500: dialogue choices, mission choices, activity choices. Play naturally and the count climbs; do not rush it, because it is the kind of trophy that pops late, near the end of a thorough playthrough. Flagged missable as a caution: a choice made cannot be unmade, so pick deliberately in story missions where the description suggests the choice matters.
trophies.missableNote: PSN counts choices to 500, and a choice cannot be unmade. Choose deliberately in story missions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try — the description suggests a retry moment: fail something once, then succeed at it on the very next attempt. The honest reading is that this pops from a specific second-attempt success, most plausibly a mission or challenge that the game lets you retry. If it has not popped on its own, try a retryable challenge: fail it once on purpose, then clear it on the second attempt. Flagged missable as a caution because a second attempt only exists where the game offers one.
trophies.missableNote: A second-try moment. If it has not popped, retry a challenge: fail once, then clear it on the next attempt.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the description reads like a random event or an easter egg: something odd happening in the world that you happen to see. There is no place or step named, so do not chase a specific spot: explore Leonida, follow unusual prompts and odd sights, and this pops when the moment finds you. Flagged missable as a caution only because a one-off random event may not repeat — if a strange event starts, stay with it until it plays out.
trophies.missableNote: A strange one-off moment. If something odd starts happening, stay with it until it plays out.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee swing from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a target on foot, swing as you pass, and the trophy pops when the hit connects. Pick a quiet street so the police response stays manageable, and expect a wanted level: this is a feat to do deliberately, not by accident. It can be retried, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts — the game's money-cleaning loop. Marked bills come from robberies and heists; pass them to your contacts to clean them, and the trophy pops when $250,000 of cleaned money has been earned. Keep the loop running alongside the crime feats in stage 5 and the total climbs on its own. It cannot be missed: contacts and marked bills stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — weapons, clothes, cars, food, anything the shops of Leonida sell. The total is cumulative across every shop, so it climbs naturally as you gear up for the other trophies; if it is still short near the end, buy the big-ticket items (vehicles and weapons) rather than small consumables. It cannot be missed: shops stay open after the story.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN tracks the count to 8. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this is a spending goal as much as a collection one: earn the cash (the laundering loop in stage 5 helps) and buy each garage as you can afford it. The trophy pops when the eighth garage is yours. It cannot be missed: properties stay buyable after the story.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game delivery app. Open the app on the in-game phone, register vehicles to it one by one, and the trophy pops at the tenth. Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones you already own or drive rather than hunting specific models. It cannot be missed: the app stays available after the story.
trophies.name: On the Spot
